newsitem.title: USA: Swedish official seeks review of IMF constitution.
newsitem.headline: Swedish official seeks review of IMF constitution.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink called on Wednesday for a review of the International Monetary Fund's governing "Articles of Agreement."
"It is not a question of if, but rather a question of when to undertake this review," he told the IMF/World Bank annual meeting. "The time is now ripe for starting serious work."

Asbrink singled out three issues for attention -- Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), capital account transactions and the IMF's method of paying its running costs. The review will have a better chance to succeed if it is limited to a few well-defined issues, he said.

The IMF is currently considering a selective allocation of its artificial currency, the SDR, mainly aimed at aiding nations that have joined the Fund since the last issue in 1981. Such a move would require an amendment to the Articles.
"The second issue is capital account convertibility," Asbrink said. "There are good arguments for reviewing the Fund's jurisdiction in this area."

The present articles permit -- and in some cases encourage -- countries to impose controls on capital account transactions. But Asbrink said, "Recent experience points to the minimal effectiveness of exchange and capital controls."

That echoed comments on Sunday by British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, who demanded a change in the Articles to encourage developing countries to open up their economies to foreign capital.
Asbrink also called for a review of the the IMF's system of financing its running costs. Those costs are now financed by borrowing countries through the rates they on their loans.
Asbrink saw "widespread interest in moving to a a more transparent and equitable system." That would presumably involve payments by creditors as well as borrowers.
